newsitem.title: UK: Gengold says "jury still out" on Beatrix hedge.
newsitem.headline: Gengold says "jury still out" on Beatrix hedge.

text.p: The "jury was still out" on the 2.9 million ounce gold hedge put in place last year to protect investments of Gencor Ltd Ltd's gold division Gengold in its Beatrix Mine development project, Gengold managing director Tom Dale said on Tuesday.
"It was put in place to protect a Rand 850 million capital project," Dale said at a presentation of the company's December quarter results.
He added that "it was highly unlikely" that they company would buy back the gold sold forward and that unlike some of its South African gold mining competitors, Gengold "was not a natural hedger".
During the quarter ended December the gold price averaged rand 56,095 per kg but the Beatrix hedge hit by the declining value of the rand realised only rand 50,763 per kg.
"It could emerge from under water this quarter," Dale said, noting that the difference between the hedge price and the realisable gold price had narrowed to Rand 1,500 per kg.
"We still think it made good business sense to hedge a long term investment like Beatrix,' another Gengold official said after the presentation.

Dale also noted that the swap arrangement between Gengold and Anglo American Corp for mineral rights in the Orange Free State and further north near the Evander mine would add about 230 tonnes of gold to Gengold's minable reserves.
The Orange Free State mines to benefit were Oryx and Beatrix, the latter of which would have its reserves increased by two million ounces from nine million ounces, Dale said.

Access to the shallowest portion of the new ore body could be achieved within about a year from underground at the Beatrix mine and a deeper area would be accessed from Beatrix's No. 3 shaft within two years, Gengold director Peter Richardson said.
"We are talking to JCI and Gold Fields of South Africa as well as other people with mineral rights in the (Beatrix) area," Dale said.
He described the talks as "very sensitive" but added that he hoped to make Beatrix's No.3 shaft an "exploration platform" for the area.
A London-based mining share analyst said after the presentation, "A few years ago a swap of mineral rights between two South African mining houses would have been impossible."
Gengold on Monday announced improved distributable income for the sixth consecutive quarter and an increase in gold production of 3.8 percent while costs were reduced by 1.7 percent.
Gold output was 10,455 kg and the average gold price realised was R55,375 per kg, 1.8 percent up on the September quarter.
Operating income rose 19.2 percent to R138.20 million compared with a 3.5 percent rise posted in the previous quarter and income after tax was R12.2 milion higher at $120.2 million.
